GBM Pipeline - Stage 3: NMD Cohort Summary

GBM NMD-Neoantigen Pipeline · github.com/paleslui/gbm-nmd-pipeline

This report summarises NMD-actionable neoantigen candidates across the cohort. The hypothesis is that TMZ-induced frameshift mutations create premature termination codons (PTCs) that are silenced by nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD); inhibiting NMD could expose these neoantigens to immune recognition. Frameshift variants are the only neoantigen class that creates novel peptides actionable by NMD inhibition; missense variants are not NMD-relevant and stop-gained variants do not produce peptide neoantigens. The variant landscape below is shown for context, but the rest of this report focuses exclusively on frameshift-derived candidates.

NMD scoring methods

Method 1 - VEP NMD plugin

The VEP NMD plugin (Ensembl v105+) annotates truncating variants with NMD_escaping_variant when the PTC is predicted to escape NMD. An empty NMD field on a truncating variant means NMD is triggered (SENSITIVE).

Method 2 - Lindeboom rules (Nat Genet 2019)

Applied to frameshift and stop-gained variants. Rules in priority order:

  • Rule 4 - Start-proximal PTC (<150 nt): Pioneer round completes before NMD surveillance → INSENSITIVE
  • Rule 1 - Last exon: No downstream EJC to trigger NMD → INSENSITIVE
  • Rule 3 - Long exon (>407 nt): EJC too far downstream → INSENSITIVE
  • Rule 2 - 55 nt boundary: PTC >55 nt upstream of last EJC → SENSITIVE (canonical NMD)

Ensemble confidence (0–3)

3 = both methods agree; 2 = single method available; 1 = methods disagree; 0 = no data.

Priority tiers

TIER 1 - NMD-sensitive + IC50 < 50 nM. Primary therapeutic targets - silenced by NMD, exposed by NMD inhibition.
TIER 2 - NMD-sensitive + IC50 50–500 nM. Moderate binders, potentially relevant after NMD inhibition.
TIER 3 - NMD-insensitive + IC50 < 500 nM. Already expressed - controls for immune response without NMD inhibition.

Note on samples vs patients: the cohort contains paired primary (T) and recurrent (M) samples, so 28 patients = 56 samples. Of the 7 samples with 0 candidates, most are paired with a non-empty timepoint in the same patient (so the patient still counts as represented). Only when both T and M timepoints are empty does a patient drop out of the cohort entirely.

Variant landscape - input candidates by type

Distribution of all 338 pVACseq candidates across the cohort. Frameshift (FS) is the only NMD-actionable variant type for neoantigen-based immunotherapy. The remaining sections of this report show NMD analysis on the 99 FS candidates only.

Fig 1. Variant type distribution. Of 338 candidates, 99 are frameshift (NMD-actionable).

Variant TypeCount% of totalNMD-actionable?
missense20660.9no
FS9929.3yes
inframe_del278.0no
inframe_ins61.8no
Why we focus on frameshift only: Missense variants are not NMD-relevant (they replace one amino acid without introducing a PTC). Stop-gained variants are NMD-relevant but truncate the protein without generating novel peptide sequences - pVACseq does not emit peptide candidates for them, so they are not actionable for neoantigen vaccines. Inframe indels do not introduce PTCs.
